preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= a for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])) and all(1 <= int(y) <= b for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints x and y are within the valid vertex ranges (1 ≤ x ≤ a, 1 ≤ y ≤ b).
The input has exactly m + 1 lines, where the first line contains a, b, m and the next m lines contain edges.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set((x, y) for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])) & {(x, y)}) == 1 for x, y in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: There are no multiple edges in the graph (each edge (x, y) appears exactly once).

postconditions.expression: stdout.splitlines()[0].strip() == str(c) and c == max(colors) if colors else 0
postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the minimal number of colors c used, where c is the maximum color value in the output.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.splitlines()[1].split()) == m and all(1 <= int(color) <= c for color in stdout.splitlines()[1].split())
postconditions.description: The second line contains exactly m integers (colors) in the same order as input edges, each between 1 and c.

postconditions.expression: all(int(color1) != int(color2) for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate((line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])) for j, (x2, y2) in enumerate((line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])) if i < j and (x1 == x2 or y1 == y2))
postconditions.description: No two adjacent edges (sharing a common vertex) have the same color.
